install_tell: Two-service OSS stack: presidio-analyzer (NER + recognizers) and presidio-anonymizer (redact/replace/hash). Python pip install presidio-analyzer / presidio-anonymizer OR docker images mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-analyzer and mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-anonymizer. Ships with NO authentication.
misconfig_patterns: PRESIDIO_ANALYZER_API_BASE defaults to plain http:// if no scheme provided (litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/presidio.py line ~187): unencrypted PII in transit between LiteLLM proxy and Presidio backends. Catastrophic default on any non-loopback deployment.

Anonymizer ships with no auth layer. Anyone reaching :5001/anonymize can submit text and receive redacted output (and infer original text via differential reconstruction with multiple operator templates).
Operators run Presidio docker images on flat networks intending 'internal only,' but Docker bind 0.0.0.0 default exposes both services to LAN.
ad_hoc_recognizers config can be a JSON file path OR an environment-loaded string; a writable ad_hoc_recognizers path is a regex-injection foothold (custom recognizers run regex against every input).

active_probe.false_positive_check: Both services return distinctive health strings; do NOT call /analyze or /anonymize with real text -- those are PII-processing endpoints.

deployment_tells: Two-service signature: :5001 (analyzer) + :5002 (anonymizer) on the same host is the Presidio tell
spaCy / NLP model bundle presence (~500MB) in associated containers
LiteLLM proxy upstream: PRESIDIO_*_API_BASE env vars in .env
pivot_paths: An exposed Presidio analyzer that an operator forwards their inference traffic through IS a passive PII sniffer for any attacker who finds it: send same text Presidio sees, observe entity types it returns, infer the operator's data classes.
Multi-service docker-compose pattern: Presidio rarely runs alone; co-located with the upstream LLM stack. Finding Presidio means finding the LLM proxy and the model backend nearby.

framework_vs_deployment.framework: github.com/microsoft/presidio (MIT, ~5k stars), arxiv research lineage; canonical OSS PII library.
framework_vs_deployment.deployment_risk: Lives in the OPERATOR. Microsoft ships the library; operators ship it as an internal service. No CVE backs this category yet; risk is policy (auth-not-shipped) not code.
framework_vs_deployment.discipline: Treat the same as LlamaFirewall / OpenGuardrails per Lane D summary: framework count, not deployment count, when reasoning about population. Dork measures operators who chose to expose; library-mode invisible.

dork_population_substitution_risk: HIGH. Same shape as Lane D summary. The Shodan-visible Presidio population is operators who shipped the docker-compose stack on a routable host without an auth shim. The much larger population imports presidio-analyzer as a Python library inside their own service; that population is invisible to passive enumeration.

added_surface: LiteLLM defaults presidio_*_api_base to http:// (not https://) when scheme is missing; PII travels unencrypted by default.
mock_testing path uses static mock_redacted_text; an operator who left mock_testing=True in production silently bypasses Presidio.

output_parse_pii expands the event_hook to include post_call; the unmask logic stores a pii_tokens mapping in proxy memory (token -> original PII). The mapping is per-instance memory; a memory-disclosing CVE in LiteLLM would dump the un-anonymization table.
ad_hoc_recognizers loaded from operator-supplied path is a config-tampering primitive for anyone with proxy filesystem write.
litellm_wrapper_delta.verdict: NOT a transparent passthrough. LiteLLM adds a pii_tokens in-memory de-anonymization table, a mock-testing bypass, and a plain-HTTP default. The Presidio OSS library itself is unchanged; the wrapper introduces meaningful new attack surface beyond the OSS framework.
